newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs close weaker on EPA report, trade minister.
newsitem.headline: JGBs close weaker on EPA report, trade minister.

text.p: The key September Japanese Government Bond (JGBs) futures ended weaker, unable to make up early losses sparked by remarks from Japan's trade minister and an annual report on the economy, traders said on Friday.
September JGBs ended at 125.04, down from Thursday's 125.14, on turnover of 33,152 contracts. The contract moved in a 124.91 to 125.24 range.
Trade Minister Shinji Sato said on Friday that Japan's current policy of keeping interest rates low was not effective.
"When interest rates are low, there should be an expansive effect on capital spending, but there is no such effect now.
"On the other hand, it has a dampening effect on the purchasing power of individuals such as pensioners, who feel that their savings are dwindling." Sato said.

Meanwhile, the government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said in its annual white paper that two years had passed since interest rates had been cut to rock-bottom levels and that firms, financial institutions and individuals should be aware there is a risk that intertest rates may rise.
The EPA, however, did not comment on whether or when interest rates should be raised.
In the cash JGB market, major city banks sold 167th and 193rd 10-year JGBs, traders said.
Those moves appear to have reflected profit-taking by the banks ahead of the three-day holiday weekend, they said.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.285 percent at 0620 GMT, up from Thursday's 2.275 percent.
The JGB market in Japan will be closed on Monday for a national holiday.
JGBs rose briefly in early trade, buoyed by declines in the Tokyo stock market, but they soon surrendered all the gains following the EPA report and the trade minister's remark.
In the Euroyen futures market, traders detected operations based on a yield-flattening strategy. Foreign accounts sold December futures for March and June, but this failed to give a boost to JGBs.
Next week the market is expected to focus on a new 10-year JGB auction scheduled on Wednesday with a prospective 2.4 to 2.5 percent coupon.
"We see little problem selling them (the new JGBs) to investors and September JGBs may challenge key resistance at 125.50 after the auction," said a brokerage trader.
